newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes little changed against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes little changed against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed little changed at 8.3010 against the U.S. dollar on Monday from 8.3009 last Friday, with no reaction to the news of a rise in China's foreign reserves, traders said.
Official media reported on the weekend that China's foreign exchange reserves reached $100.45 billion on November 12.
Dealers said the rise in foreign exchange reserves would give the central bank more control over the yuan's movement. But it had no direct effect on trading today, they said.
The yuan opened slightly up at an intra-day high of 8.3005 and moved down to consolidate between 8.3010 and 8.3015 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.3019.
Trading was active, with most done at 8.3012, traders said.

"The rise of reserves had little impact on the yuan's stable movement today," one dealer said. "But it implied that the central bank has been continuously buying dollars in the market, which prevented the yuan from rising further."
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.3010 on Tuesday.
The yuan closed slightly up at 7.2930 from 7.2943 against 100 Japanese yen and sharply higher at an intra-day high of 1.0720 from 1.0741 against the Hong Kong dollar.
